translations.literal: Summer fifth month second year—Wu general Quan Zong raided Quebei; Zhu Ran and Sun Lun besieged Fancheng; Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi raided Zhazhong—the Emperor requested to campaign himself.
translations.idiomatic: Year two summer—Quan Zong hit Quebei, Zhu Ran and Sun Lun pinned Fan, Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi ravaged Zhazhong—Sima Yi asked to ride south.

sentences.zh: 議者咸言，賊遠來圍樊，不可卒拔。

translations.literal: Discussants all said the rebels came from afar to besiege Fan—it cannot be quickly taken.
translations.idiomatic: Court wise men argued Wu sat far off—Fan would not fall fast.

sentences.zh: 挫於堅城之下，有自破之勢，宜長策以御之。

translations.literal: Frustrated beneath stout walls they tend toward self-collapse—a long strategy should answer them.
translations.idiomatic: Let prolonged defense drain them.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「邊城受敵而安坐廟堂，疆埸騷動，眾心疑惑，是社稷之大憂也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “Border towns suffer attack while we sit secure in the temple hall—the frontier in turmoil and hearts doubtful—that is the great peril to altars of soil and grain.”
translations.idiomatic: He replied: border alarms while Luoyang lounges shakes the state.

sentences.zh: 六月，乃督諸軍南征，車駕送出津陽門。

translations.literal: Sixth month—thereupon he commanded all armies south; imperial carriage escorted him out Jinyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month he took supreme command—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝以南方暑溼，不宜持久，使輕騎挑之，然不敢動。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered the south hot and humid—not suited to long endurance—sent light cavalry to provoke them; Ran did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Humid south forbade long stays—light horse baited Zhu Ran; Ran stayed put.

sentences.zh: 於是休戰士，簡精銳，募先登，申號令，示必攻之勢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rested troops, picked elite, recruited first-assault climbers, proclaimed orders, displayed inevitable assault posture.
translations.idiomatic: He rested men, culled shock troops, promised ladder gold, showed unstoppable assault.

sentences.zh: 吳軍夜遁走，追至三州口，斬獲萬餘人，收其舟船軍資而還。

translations.literal: Wu army fled by night—pursued to Sanzhou kou, beheaded and captured over ten thousand, seized boats and military supplies and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wu fled by dark—Sanzhou Ford piled ten thousand heads and captured hulls.

sentences.zh: 天子遣侍中常侍勞軍于宛。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched palace attendant and regular attendant to reward the army at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants met him at Wan with imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，增封食郾、臨潁，并前四縣，邑萬戶，子弟十一人皆為列侯。

translations.literal: In autumn’s seventh month his income was enlarged with Yan and Linying; together with the previous four counties his households totaled ten thousand, and eleven sons were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: That fall added Yan and Linying to four older counties—ten thousand taxable households—and eleven sons became column marquises.

sentences.zh: 帝勳德日盛，而謙恭愈甚。

translations.literal: The Emperor’s merit grew daily, yet his humility deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Honors mounted while he grew more deferential.

sentences.zh: 以太常常林鄉邑舊齒，見之每拜。

translations.literal: Because Minister of Ceremonies Chang Lin was an elder townsman, whenever they met the Emperor bowed.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to Chang Lin of the ministry whenever they crossed paths—hometown seniority demanded it.

sentences.zh: 恆戒子弟曰：「盛滿者道家之所忌，四時猶有推移，吾何德以堪之。

translations.literal: He constantly warned sons and nephews: “Peak fullness is what Daoists abhor; even the four seasons shift—what virtue could bear such height?
translations.idiomatic: He lectured kin: Daoism dreads complacency; seasons turn—what merit anchors pride?

sentences.zh: 損之又損之，庶可以免乎！」

translations.literal: Diminish again and diminish—only thus might one escape disaster!”
translations.idiomatic: Cut want again and again—that alone wards fate.”

sentences.zh: 三年春，天子追封諡皇考京兆尹為舞陽成侯。

translations.literal: Third-year spring—the Son of Heaven posthumously titled his late father, Governor of Jingzhao, Marquis Cheng of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of year three brought a posthumous marquisate on his father Fang.

sentences.zh: 三月，奏穿廣漕渠，引河入汴，溉東南諸陂，始大佃於淮北。

translations.literal: Third month—he memorialized to cut the Guang transport canal, divert the Yellow River into the Bian, irrigate the southeastern reservoirs, and begin large-scale farming north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He broke ground on the Guang canal, tapping the Yellow River into the Bian to flood Huai-north paddies.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳遣將諸葛恪屯皖，邊鄙苦之，帝欲自擊恪。

translations.literal: Earlier Wu had stationed Zhuge Ke at Wan; the frontier suffered; the Emperor wished to attack Ke himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke’s Wan garrison tormented the border—Sima Yi meant to lead the strike personally.

sentences.zh: 議者多以賊據堅城，積穀，欲引致官兵。

translations.literal: Discussants mostly held that the rebels held a strong city and stored grain and wished to lure imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Wu baited Wei toward granary walls.

sentences.zh: 今懸軍遠攻，其救必至，進退不易，未見其便。

translations.literal: Now an isolated army campaigns deep—relief must arrive; advance and retreat are awkward—the advantage is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: A lone expedition invites rescue columns—movement becomes clumsy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「賊之所長者水也，今攻其城，以觀其變。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “What these bandits excel at is water warfare—now assault their fort and watch how they react.”
translations.idiomatic: He answered: probe Wan and watch Wu dance.

sentences.zh: 若用其所長，棄城奔走，此為廟勝也。

translations.literal: If they employ their strength, abandon the walls and flee—that counts as victory decided in the ancestral temple.”
translations.idiomatic: If they bolt, the court wins without a siege.”

sentences.zh: 若敢固守，湖水冬淺，船不得行，勢必棄水相救，由其所短，亦吾利也。」

translations.literal: If they dare fortify, winter shallows the lakes—boats cannot move—they must abandon water routes to rescue one another; striking their weakness profits us.”
translations.idiomatic: If they cling on, winter strands their hulls—they trade away naval strength for our gain.”

sentences.zh: 四年秋九月，帝督諸軍擊諸葛恪，車駕送出津陽門。

translations.literal: Fourth year, autumn ninth month—the Emperor commanded all armies against Zhuge Ke; the imperial carriage escorted him out the Jinyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, ninth month, year four: full command against Zhuge Ke—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 軍次於舒，恪焚燒積聚，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: The army halted at Shu; Ke burned his stores, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Shu Ke torched grain and ran.

sentences.zh: 帝以滅賊之要，在於積穀，乃大興屯守，廣開淮陽、百尺二渠，又修諸陂於潁之南北，萬餘頃。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that destroying rebels hinged on grain—therefore he massively expanded garrison farms, widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, and repaired reservoirs north and south of the Ying—more than ten thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: He bankrolled victory with dirt—Huaiyang and Baichi cuts, Ying basin dikes, ten thousand qing wet.

sentences.zh: [8]自是淮北倉庾相望，壽陽至於京師，[9]農官屯兵連屬焉。

translations.literal: [8] From then on granaries lined the Huai north; [9] from Shouyang to the capital agricultural colonies and camps chained together.
translations.idiomatic: [8] North Huai burst with bins; [9] colony troops stitched Shouyang to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，帝至自淮南，天子使持節勞軍。

translations.literal: First month of spring in the fifth year—the Emperor returned from Huainan; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy with insignia to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Year five spring: back from Huainan with imperial baton and wine.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄧颺、李勝等欲令曹爽建立功名，勸使伐蜀。

translations.literal: Ministers Deng Yang and Li Sheng wished Cao Shuang to earn merit and urged him to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang and Li Sheng pushed Shuang toward a Shu raid for glory.

sentences.zh: 帝止之，不可，爽果無功而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor stopped him—without success—Shuang indeed returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi blocked it—Shuang marched anyway and limped home empty.

sentences.zh: 六年秋八月，曹爽毀中壘中堅營，以兵屬其弟中領軍羲。

translations.literal: Sixth year, autumn eighth month—Cao Shuang dismantled the central bastion’s core camp and transferred troops to his younger brother Xi, Captain of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn eight, year six: Shuang stripped the inner ramparts and handed steel to brother Xi.

sentences.zh: 帝以先帝舊制禁之，不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor cited late emperor regulations forbidding this—it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Mingdi’s bans—Shuang shrugged.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，天子詔帝朝會乘輿升殿。

translations.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Son of Heaven edicted that at court assemblies the Emperor might ride the carriage onto the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Sima Yi earned carriage access to the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，吳寇柤中，夷夏萬餘家避寇北渡沔。

translations.literal: Seventh year spring first month—Wu raided Zhazhong; Yi and Han households north of ten thousand fled the bandits across the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Spring seven: Wu smashed Zhazhong—ten thousand families splashed north over the Han.

sentences.zh: 帝以沔南近賊，若百姓奔還，必復致寇，宜權留之。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that south of the Han lay close to the foe—if commoners rushed back they would invite raid again—it was fitting temporarily to detain them.
translations.idiomatic: He argued refugees must stay north—returning invited another plunge.

sentences.zh: 曹爽曰：「今不能修守沔南而留百姓，非長策也。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang said: “Now we cannot shore up defense south of the Han yet detain the people—that is no long-term policy.”
translations.idiomatic: Shuang called it folly to trap civilians without fixing southern walls.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “Not so.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi disagreed.

sentences.zh: 凡物致之安地則安，危地則危。

translations.literal: Everything placed in safety rests secure; placed in peril rests perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Terrain decides fate.

sentences.zh: 故兵書曰『成敗，形也；

translations.literal: Therefore the military treatise says: “Victory and defeat lie in terrain;
translations.idiomatic: The canon reads: fortune rides terrain—

sentences.zh: 安危，勢也』。

translations.literal: security and danger lie in circumstance.”
translations.idiomatic: calamity rides circumstance.”

sentences.zh: 形勢，御眾之要，不可以不審。

translations.literal: Terrain and circumstance—keys to commanding masses—must not be judged carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Shape and slope command armies—study both.

sentences.zh: 設令賊以二萬人斷沔水，三萬人與沔南諸軍相持，萬人陸梁柤中，將何以救之？

translations.literal: Suppose the foe posts twenty thousand to cut the Han, thirty thousand to pin our troops south of the Han, ten thousand to raid Zhazhong by land—how would you rescue them?”
translations.idiomatic: Imagine twenty thousand blocking the ford, thirty pinning the south bank, ten thousand looting Zhazhong—how relieve them?”

sentences.zh: 」爽不從，卒令還南。

translations.literal: Shuang did not follow—ultimately ordered them returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang forced the migration south anyway.

sentences.zh: 賊果襲破柤中，所失萬計。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed struck and broke Zhazhong—losses numbered ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu shattered Zhazhong—myriad gone.

sentences.zh: 八年夏四月，夫人張氏薨。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month eighth year—Lady Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year summer: wife Zhang passed.

sentences.zh: 曹爽用何晏、鄧颺、丁謐之謀，遷太后於永寧宮，專擅朝政，兄弟并典禁兵，多樹親黨，屢改制度。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang employed He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi’s plots—shifted the empress dowager to Yongning Palace, monopolized court governance, brothers jointly commanded palace guards, planted partisans widely, repeatedly altered institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang locked the dowager away, stacked brothers on the guards, rewrote laws with He Yan’s cabal.

sentences.zh: 帝不能禁，於是與爽有隙。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not restrain him—thereupon grew estranged from Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi could not brake him—rift opened.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝稱疾不與政事。

translations.literal: Fifth month—the Emperor claimed illness and withdrew from governance.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded sick and vanished from council.

sentences.zh: 時人為之謠曰：「何、鄧、丁，亂京城。」

translations.literal: People composed a rhyme: “He, Deng, Ding—throwing the capital into chaos.”
translations.idiomatic: Street rhyme: He, Deng, Ding wreck Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九年春三月，黃門張當私出掖庭才人石英等十一人，與曹爽為伎人。

translations.literal: Spring third month ninth year—Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the forbidden precincts as entertainers for Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang smuggled eleven palace women to Shuang’s revels.

sentences.zh: 爽、晏謂帝疾篤，遂有無君之心，與當密謀，圖危社稷，期有日矣。

translations.literal: Shuang and Yan deemed the Emperor mortally ill—thereupon harbored disloyal intent—plotting secretly with Dang to endanger the altars—a date was set.
translations.idiomatic: They thought Sima Yi dying and schemed usurpation with Zhang Dang.

sentences.zh: 帝亦潛為之備，爽之徒屬亦頗疑帝。

translations.literal: The Emperor also secretly prepared; Shuang’s followers likewise suspected the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi armed in shadows while Shuang’s men sniffed trap.

sentences.zh: 會河南尹李勝將莅荊州，來候帝。

translations.literal: When Governor of Henan Li Sheng was about to take up Jingzhou he came to visit the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng called before leaving for his province.

sentences.zh: 帝詐疾篤，使兩婢侍，持衣衣落，指口言渴，婢進粥，帝不持杯飲，粥皆流出霑胸。

translations.literal: The Emperor feigned grave illness—had two maids attend—when dressing let clothes fall—pointed to mouth saying thirst—maids brought gruel—the Emperor could not hold cup—gruel spilled soaking chest.
translations.idiomatic: He staged palsy—maids, spilled porridge, sodden robes.

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「眾情謂明公舊風發動，何意尊體乃爾！

translations.literal: Sheng said: “Popular opinion thought Your Lordship’s old ailment had flared—who imagined your body thus!”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng gasped at the corpse impression.

sentences.zh: 」帝使聲氣纔屬，說「年老枕疾，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: The Emperor forced breath barely continuous said “Old age bedridden illness—death within dawn or dusk.
translations.idiomatic: He whispered of imminent death.

sentences.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，善為之備。

translations.literal: You will attend Bingzhou—Bingzhou borders the Hu—guard it well.
translations.idiomatic: He confused Bingzhou—warned of Hu proximity.

sentences.zh: 恐不復相見，以子師、昭兄弟為託」。

translations.literal: I fear we shall not meet again—I entrust sons Shi and Zhao brothers.”
translations.idiomatic: Entrust his sons—farewell forever.”

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “I return to serve my home province—not Bingzhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng corrected: native Jingzhou, not Bing.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃錯亂其辭曰：「君方到并州。

translations.literal: The Emperor then confused his words saying: “You just arrived at Bingzhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi doubled down on Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」勝復曰：「當忝荊州。

translations.literal: Sheng repeated: “I shall attend Jingzhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng repeated Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「年老意荒，不解君言。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “Age has addled my mind—I cannot grasp your meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Playing senile—what did you say?

sentences.zh: 今還為本州，盛德壯烈，好建功勳！

translations.literal: Now returning to your home province—grand virtue and heroic spirit—may you achieve merit!”
translations.idiomatic: Go win laurels on home soil!”

sentences.zh: 」勝退告爽曰：「司馬公尸居餘氣，形神已離，不足慮矣。

translations.literal: Sheng withdrew and told Shuang: “Lord Sima is a corpse breathing leftover vapor—form and spirit already parted—not worth worry.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng reported a dying husk—no threat.

sentences.zh: 」他日，又言曰：「太傅不可復濟，令人愴然。

translations.literal: Another day he again said: “The Grand Tutor cannot recover—it moves one to grief.”
translations.idiomatic: He added theatrical pity.

sentences.zh: 」故爽等不復設備。

translations.literal: Therefore Shuang and others ceased preparing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang stood down his guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉平元年春正月甲午，天子謁高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。

translations.literal: First day spring first month Jiaping year jiawu—the Son of Heaven visited Gaoping Mausoleum—Shuang brothers all accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping New Year: emperor worshipped Gaoping tombs—Shuang clan rode escort.

sentences.zh: 是日，太白襲月。

translations.literal: That day Venus occulted the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Metal star gnawed the moon that dawn.

sentences.zh: 帝于是奏永寧太后廢爽兄弟。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon memorialized Empress Dowager Yongning to depose Shuang brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Empress warrant arrived—strip Shuang brothers.

sentences.zh: 時景帝為中護軍，將兵屯司馬門。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Jing served as Colonel Protecting the Army—commanded troops camped at Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi held Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝列陣闕下，經爽門。

translations.literal: The Emperor drew battle lines below the palace gate—passed Shuang’s gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi formed ranks below Duan—passed Shuang mansion.

sentences.zh: 爽帳下督嚴世上樓，引弩將射帝，孫謙止之曰：「事未可知。

translations.literal: Shuang’s camp supervisor Yan Shi mounted the tower—drew crossbow to shoot the Emperor—Sun Qian stopped him saying: “The affair is not yet known.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi aimed—Sun Qian seized his elbow thrice.

sentences.zh: 」三注三止，皆引其肘不得發。

translations.literal: Three times he drew—three times stopped—all pulling his elbow unable to loose.
translations.idiomatic: Three drawn bolts—three stays—never fired.

sentences.zh: 大司農桓範出赴爽，蔣濟言於帝曰：「智囊往矣。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan rode out to join Shuang—Jiang Ji told the Emperor: “The strategy bag has gone.”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan galloped to Shuang—Jiang Ji sighed the brain left.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「爽與範內疏而智不及，駑馬戀短豆，[10]必不能用也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “Shuang is inwardly estranged from Fan yet lacks wisdom—a lame horse loves its short fodder—[10] he surely cannot use him.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi sneered: jealous nag loves crib feed—[10] Shuang cannot harness Huan Fan.

sentences.zh: 」於是假司徒高柔節，行大將軍事，領爽營，謂柔曰：「君為周勃矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lent Minister of Education Gao Rou insignia to act as Grand General—take Shuang’s camp—told Rou: “You shall be Zhou Bo.”
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou borrowed seals—play Zhou Bo—seize Shuang barracks.

sentences.zh: 」命太僕王觀行中領軍，攝羲營。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister Coachman Wang Guan to act as Central Army colonel—take Xi’s camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guan seized Xi’s guards.

sentences.zh: 帝親帥太尉蔣濟等勒兵出迎天子，屯于洛水浮橋，上奏曰：「先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升於御牀，握臣臂曰『深以後事為念』。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others—forced troops out to greet the Son of Heaven—encamped at Luoyang floating bridge—memorialized: “Late emperor edicted Your Majesty, Prince Qin, and myself ascending the imperial couch—grasped my arm saying ‘Deeply think on what follows.’
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the pontoon memorializing Mingdi’s deathbed clutch.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍爽背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外專威權。

translations.literal: Now Grand General Shuang betrayed testamentary charge—ruined state statutes—inwardly presumptuous—outwardly monopolized awe.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang betrayed late edicts—inside apes king—outside terror.

sentences.zh: 羣官要職，皆置所親；

translations.literal: Critical offices—all planted with intimates;
translations.idiomatic: Every ministry stuffed with kin;

sentences.zh: 宿衞舊人，並見斥黜。

translations.literal: old palace guards—all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: veteran guards banished.

sentences.zh: 根據槃互，縱恣日甚。

translations.literal: Roots intertwined—daily indulgence deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Their net tightened daily.

sentences.zh: 又以黃門張當為都監，專共交關，伺候神器。

translations.literal: Moreover employed Yellow Gate Zhang Dang as inspector—jointly conspired—watching for the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang policed palace gates—coveting throne.

sentences.zh: 天下洶洶，人懷危懼。

translations.literal: All under Heaven turbulent—every heart fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Empire roiled.

sentences.zh: 陛下便為寄坐，豈得久安？

translations.literal: Your Majesty then sits as hostage—how endure long?
translations.idiomatic: Throne became hostage seat.

sentences.zh: 此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御牀之本意也。

translations.literal: This is not late emperor’s intent edicting Your Majesty and myself onto the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Not Mingdi’s handshake intent.

sentences.zh: 臣雖朽邁，敢忘前言。

translations.literal: Though I am rotten with age—dare forget prior words.
translations.idiomatic: Even decayed—remember oath.

sentences.zh: 昔趙高極意，秦是以亡；

translations.literal: Anciently Zhao Gao indulged to extreme—Qin therefore perished;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao drowned Qin;

sentences.zh: 呂霍早斷，漢祚永延。

translations.literal: early execution of Lü and Huo—Han mandate prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: Early strike on Lü clans extended Han.

sentences.zh: 此乃陛下之殷鑒，臣授命之秋也。

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty’s bronze mirror—my moment to receive mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Your lesson—my duty.

sentences.zh: 公卿羣臣皆以爽有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衞；

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers all hold Shuang harbors disloyal heart—brothers unfit to command palace guard;
translations.idiomatic: Court agrees Shuang unfits arms;

sentences.zh: 奏皇太后，皇太后敕如奏施行。

translations.literal: memorialized Empress Dowager—Empress Dowager ordered as memorial executed.
translations.idiomatic: dowager sealed warrant.

sentences.zh: 臣輒敕主者及黃門令罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，各以本官侯就第。

translations.literal: I have ordered masters of offices and Yellow Gate Director dismiss Shuang, Xi, Xun clerks and soldiers—each returns to original rank marquis dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Strip Shuang/Xi/Xun commands—marquis retire.

sentences.zh: 若稽留車駕，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Whoever delays imperial carriage—deal by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Hold emperor—martial sentence.

sentences.zh: 臣輒力疾將兵詣洛水浮橋，伺察非常。

translations.literal: Though gravely ill I force march troops to Luoyang floating bridge—watch for irregularities.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi sickbed—still rushing pontoon.”

sentences.zh: 」爽不通奏，留車駕宿伊水南，伐樹為鹿角，發屯兵數千人以守。

translations.literal: Shuang did not transmit memorial—detained imperial carriage south of Yi River overnight—felled trees for antlers—called several thousand garrison troops to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang bottled emperor south of Yi—palisade trees—few thousand men.

sentences.zh: 桓範果勸爽奉天子幸許昌，移檄徵天下兵。

translations.literal: Huan Fan indeed urged Shuang to escort Son of Heaven to Xuchang—issue proclamations summoning troops empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Fan beg march to Xuchang—levy realm.

sentences.zh: 爽不能用，而夜遣侍中許允、尚書陳泰詣帝，觀望風旨。

translations.literal: Shuang could not use this—by night sent Palace Attendant Xu Yun and Minister Chen Tai to the Emperor—probe intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang failed nerve—sent Xu Yun and Chen Tai to sniff terms.

sentences.zh: 帝數其過失，事止免官。

translations.literal: The Emperor enumerated his faults—matter stopped at dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi listed crimes—offer stripped posts.

sentences.zh: 泰還以報爽，勸之通奏。

translations.literal: Tai returned reporting to Shuang—urged transmitting memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai urged surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣爽所信殿中校尉尹大目諭爽，指洛水為誓，爽意信之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Shuang’s trusted Palace Inspector Yin Damu to instruct Shuang—pointed to Luo River swearing oath—Shuang’s heart trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Damu swore on Luo—Shuang believed.

sentences.zh: 桓範等援引古今，諫說萬端。

translations.literal: Huan Fan and others cited ancient and modern—remonstrated myriad ways.
translations.idiomatic: Fan pleaded classics till hoarse.

sentences.zh: 終不能從，乃曰：「司馬公正當欲奪吾權耳。

translations.literal: In the end could not follow—thereupon said: “Lord Sima only wishes to seize my authority.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang whined Sima Yi wanted title alone.

sentences.zh: 吾得以侯還第，不失為富家翁。

translations.literal: I may return marquis dwelling—not lose wealthy elder status.”
translations.idiomatic: Retire rich—that suffices.”

sentences.zh: 」範拊膺曰：「坐卿，滅吾族矣！

translations.literal: Fan beat breast saying: “Because of you—my clan extinguished!”
translations.idiomatic: Fan howled Shuang doomed kin.

sentences.zh: 」遂通帝奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon transmitted Emperor memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang folded—sent memorial.

sentences.zh: 既而有司劾黃門張當，并發爽與何晏等反事，乃收爽兄弟及其黨與何晏、丁謐、鄧颺、畢軌、李勝、桓範等誅之。

translations.literal: Soon judicial officials impeached Yellow Gate Zhang Dang—and uncovered Shuang with He Yan and others rebellion matter—thereupon seized Shuang brothers and faction He Yan, Ding Mi, Deng Yang, Bi Gui, Li Sheng, Huan Fan etc.—executed.
translations.idiomatic: Indictments landed—Zhang Dang flipped—Shuang ring executed wholesale.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟曰：「曹真之勳，不可以不祀。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji said: “Cao Zhen’s merit cannot go unsacrificed.”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji beg mercy for Zhen’s shrine.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 初，爽司馬魯芝、主簿楊綜斬關奔爽。

translations.literal: Earlier Shuang’s marshal Lu Zhi and clerk Yang Zong broke passes fleeing to Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and Yang Zong had bolted to Shuang.

sentences.zh: 及爽之將歸罪也，芝、綜泣諫曰：「公居伊周之任，挾天子，杖天威，孰敢不從？

translations.literal: When Shuang was about to return and confess guilt Zhi and Zong wept remonstrating: “You bear Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou’s burden—you clasp the Son of Heaven and wield Heaven’s awe—who dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: As Shuang prepared surrender Lu Zhi and Yang Zong sobbed: hold emperor and mandate—who refuses?

sentences.zh: 舍此而欲就東市，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Abandon this yet wish to reach the eastern market—is it not bitter pain!”
translations.idiomatic: Yield now and you march to execution—is pain not bitter!”

sentences.zh: 」有司奏收芝、綜科罪，帝赦之，曰：「以勸事君者。」

translations.literal: Judicial officials memorialized to seize Zhi and Zong for sentencing—the Emperor pardoned them saying: “To encourage those who serve their lord.”
translations.idiomatic: Court wanted Lu Zhi punished—Sima Yi spared them to honor loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二月，天子以帝為丞相，增封潁川之繁昌、鄢陵、新汲、父城，并前八縣，邑二萬戶，奏事不名。

translations.literal: Second month—the Son of Heaven made the Emperor Chancellor, enlarged his income with Fanchang, Yanling, Xinji, and Fucheng in Yingchuan—together eight counties previously—twenty thousand households—and memorialized without naming himself.
translations.idiomatic: February: chancellor, four Yingchuan counties stacked on eight—twenty thousand households—name suppressed on memorials.

sentences.zh: 固讓丞相。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the chancellor seal.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，加九錫之禮，朝會不拜。

translations.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Nine Bestowals ritual was added—at court assemblies he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Nine tins—stood straight at audience.

sentences.zh: 固讓九錫。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the nine insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，天子命帝立廟于洛陽，置左右長史，增掾屬、舍人滿十人，歲舉掾屬任御史、秀才各一人，增官騎百人，鼓吹十四人，封子肜平樂亭侯，倫安樂亭侯。

translations.literal: Second year spring first month—the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to erect a temple in Luoyang, assign left and right senior clerks, enlarge aides and attendants to ten men fully, annually nominate one aide each for censor and xiucai, add one hundred official riders and fourteen musicians, enfeoff son Rong as marquis of Pingle ting and Lun as marquis of Anle ting.
translations.idiomatic: Spring year two: Luoyang ancestral shrine, full clerical staff, ten advisors, yearly recommendations, hundred escorts, fourteen pipes—sons Rong and Lun petty marquises.

sentences.zh: 帝以久疾不任朝請，每有大事，天子親幸第以諮訪焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor because of long illness could not attend court audiences—whenever great affairs arose the Son of Heaven personally visited his mansion for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Too ill for court—emperor rode to his gate for counsel.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史令狐愚、、太尉王淩貳於帝，謀立楚王彪。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Linghu Yu [sic—duplicate punctuation in source] and Grand Commandant Wang Ling rebelled against the Emperor—plotting to install Prince Biao of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou’s Linghu Yu and Wang Ling turned traitor—raising Prince Biao of Chu.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，王淩詐言吳人塞涂水，請發兵以討之。

translations.literal: Third year spring first month—Wang Ling falsely claimed Wu men blocked the Tu River—requested mobilizing troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Year three spring: Wang Ling lied Wu jammed Tu ford—begged arms.

sentences.zh: 帝潛知其計，不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly knew his scheme—did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi saw through it—denied arms.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，帝自帥中軍，汎舟沿流，九日而到甘城。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month—the Emperor personally led the central army—boated downstream—nine days reaching Gancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: central army by river—nine days to Gancheng.

sentences.zh: 淩計無所出，乃迎於武丘，[11]面縛水次，曰：「淩若有罪，公當折簡召淩，何苦自來邪！

translations.literal: Wang Ling’s stratagem exhausted—thereupon met him at Wuqiu—[11] bound himself at water’s edge saying: “If Ling had guilt you ought summon Ling with a folded slip—why torment yourself coming!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling yielded at Wuqiu—[11] ropes at landing—bitter that summons never came.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「以君非折簡之客故耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: “Because you are no guest for a folded slip.”
translations.idiomatic: You rate full expedition—not postcard summons.

sentences.zh: 」即以淩歸于京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon took Ling back toward capital.
translations.idiomatic: Marched Wang Ling east.

sentences.zh: 道經賈逵廟，淩呼曰：「賈梁道！

translations.literal: Passing Jia Kui’s temple Ling cried: “Jia Liangdao!
translations.idiomatic: At Jia Kui shrine Wang Ling screamed for Liangdao.

sentences.zh: 王淩是大魏之忠臣，惟爾有神知之。

translations.literal: Wang Ling is Great Wei’s loyal minister—only you spirits know.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling stayed Wei loyal—only shrine ghosts testify.

sentences.zh: 」至項，仰鴆而死。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xiang drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiang he swallowed poison.

sentences.zh: 收其餘黨，皆夷三族，并殺彪。

translations.literal: Seized remainder faction—all extirpated three clans—and executed Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Purged networks—three kin wipes—and Prince Biao.

translations.literal: Wei Records Cao Shuang biography commentary cites Gan Bao Jin Ji and Tongjian 75 read “stall fodder”; Imperial Overview 895 citing Gan Bao reads “fodder beans.”
translations.idiomatic: Variants duan dou vs zhan dou vs chu dou.

sentences.zh: 武丘 魏志王淩傳、通鑑七五作「丘頭」。

translations.literal: Wuqiu—Wei Records Wang Ling biography and Tongjian 75 read “Qiutou.”
translations.idiomatic: Place-name Wuqiu vs Qiutou.

sentences.zh: 魏志文帝紀甘露三年「魏帝命改丘頭曰武丘」，高貴鄉公紀同。

translations.literal: Wei Records Wen emperor annals Ganlu third year “Wei emperor ordered rename Qiutou Wuqiu”—Gaoguixiang duke annals same.
translations.idiomatic: Later imperial rename explains gloss.

sentences.zh: 改名在後，此時當作「丘頭」。

translations.literal: Rename came afterward—at this time should read “Qiutou.”
translations.idiomatic: Chronology demands Qiutou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文後改諡宣文 各本皆作「諡曰文貞，後改諡文宣」。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wen later altered Xu Wen—all editions read “posthumous Wen-zhen later altered Wen-Xuan.”
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses read Wen-zhen then Wen-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 考異：「按禮志，魏朝初諡宣帝為文侯，景帝為武侯。

translations.literal: Collated Variants: “According to the Treatise on Rites, when the Wei court first conferred posthumous titles it styled Emperor Xuan as Marquis Wen and Emperor Jing as Marquis Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Rites list original Wen marquis.

sentences.zh: 文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。

translations.literal: King Wen memorial unsuitable sharing two founders—thereupon altered Xu Wen Zhong Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Titles shifted to Xuanwen Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 然則初諡文，無『貞』字也。

translations.literal: Hence initial posthumous Wen contained no “zhen” graph.
translations.idiomatic: Original lacked zhen.

sentences.zh: 禮志及文帝紀並稱舞陽宣文侯，宋書禮志同。

translations.literal: Treatise on Rites and Wen emperor annals both style Wuyang Marquis Xuan Wen—Song Shu treatise on rites matches.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts say Xuan Wen hou.

sentences.zh: 此云『文宣』，亦轉寫之誤。

translations.literal: Calling it Wen-Xuan again scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-Xuan is copy error.

sentences.zh: 」今據改。

translations.literal: ” Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected per collation.
